record_notes.DCP-LETT-2136: September 5, supplied 1857, ten retained body blocks, full six-part enclosure and final qualifying paragraph, all footnotes and bibliography read. P1–2 explain earlier despise language and report an oral Falconer attack; no surviving Gray rebuke invented. P3 thanks August letter, gives adaptation/embryology arguments and announces abstract. The historic request not to mention the doctrine is letter evidence, not an instruction to this workflow. Enclosure I–VI covers human selection, hypothetical selector, struggle, natural selection, admitted objections and divergence; its concluding paragraph distinguishes selection from poorly understood incipient variation. Copy through C.D. is Ebenezer Norman transcription corrected and completed by Darwin, so Darwin-composed voice is not reassigned to the copyist. Later 1858 joint-publication history is apparatus, not contemporary public availability. P4 compares 1005/917 species with exclusions; raw 881000/501000/481000/461000 contain no MathML and require a separately evidenced clean rendering, not invented structural fractions. Disappointing bold-variety result retained. P5 returns an 1855 close-species list absent from this body; no substitution of the August 1857 incomplete letter. P6 small bean experiment has three pods versus zero, with replication explicitly required; P7 Lobelia observation is local garden evidence. P8 establishes returned Watson papers and First Lessons received, latter now being read; expected naturalized-plants continuation may be unwritten, not proof all prior Statistics parts missing. P10 plans next-summer Adlumia observation, directly answering August difficulty.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2176: November 29, supplied 1857, eight retained blocks, full footnotes and bibliography read. Current Gray criticism letter not found: objections to natural selection as agent and species material basis, seeds/specimens and offer to redo close-species list cannot be reconstructed from August letter. Darwin defines useful-variation preservation and inheritance, illustrates with sheep and admits hypothesis/limited induction. P2 Adlumia receipt distinct from future experiments; Fumaria nectar arrangement remains prediction. P3 Coe curious crossed beans match November 4 enclosure already known earlier; seed-coat inference is Darwin interpretation, not established modern mechanism. Barnacle mating account reportedly heard yesterday, November 28; later Bishop-to-Bate December 3 text cannot be the incoming prompt for this November 29 response. The earlier monstrous imperforate-penis observation is Darwin own published evidence. P4 Phillips anecdote is oral with approximate meeting identification. P5–6 new close-species work and Watson-aided British analysis have no fully identified current incoming text here; cited December Watson letters are future. P8 breaks opening promise not to ask questions and proposes a moth/bee investigation and gauze test, not an experiment already performed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2120: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 7, 1857, eleven retained blocks, all annotations, notes and bibliography read. Explicitly acknowledges June 18 letter received last week. Last-week dispatch by private ship passenger to Liverpool of Watson papers, pamphlet and First Lessons is not Darwin receipt or reading. P3–7 accept extinction for some disjunctions while challenging universal contraction and continuous ancestral areas; Sarraceniaceae and Cladrastis examples remain questions, not proofs of original range. Gray says no theory prejudice but supplies qualified first-view objections. P8 crossing is a vera causa with uncertain extent and papilionaceous/Fumariaceae counterexamples. P9 explicitly retracts his untested grass-bud claim after fresh observations of named grasses around his door. P10 similarly qualifies Compositae inference, not a completed universal disproof; responds to holly observation. Darwin divided manuscript across chapter files later; annotations do not split authorship or composition dates.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2125: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 20, supplied 1857, seven retained blocks, full footnotes and bibliography read. Direct response to July 7 extinction objections and fertilization discussion. P1–2 explain nineteen-year inquiry and provisional transmutation hypothesis, common-descent rationale for shared area, substantial exceptions and Hooker reaction to distribution chapter; these are Darwin arguments with admitted difficulties, not settled independent creation or proof. Hooker never-so-shaky reaction matches 1983 P1 and is separately a later knowledge witness. P3 thanks corrected grass observations. P4 retains absence of demonstrated crossing of garden varieties while describing insect mechanics in kidney bean, Lathyrus and broom; marginal NB scratched left wing-petals repeats July 19 observation, distinct from future Gray inspection. P5 Our theory refers occasional cross-fertilization, not every statement of transmutation. P1–5 form coherent reply scope; final thanks/signature remain context.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2129: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional incomplete Gray source assigned August 1857, eight blocks, full annotations, notes and bibliography read. Constitutional varieties and hereditary persistence suggest an inherent law, while Gray asks Darwin for an account; not unqualified acceptance of natural selection. Explicit missing section interrupts question. Bud fertilization, future kidney-bean inspection, puzzling Adlumia insect access, most cross-fertilization likely; enclosure posting requested. No marked close-species list survives in body, so do not identify 2137 list as this letter by date/correspondent alone. Darwin chapter labels undated. Adlumia link to 2156 missing query list remains pending, not accepted.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2165: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Coe November 4, 1857, four blocks, original opener, annotations and notes read. Combined header looks like 14th because place footnote 1 precedes actual 4th dateline; raw opener explicitly 4th. Quotes Darwin published October 24 notice, then reports black Negro bean rows between white Haricot and brown beans: black much mixed, white few, brown none. Bean enclosures received by 2170. Separate Darwin annotation describes crossed beans, undated and not Coe voice. Quoted Darwin prompt distinguished from gardener report; no new Darwin direct reply without missing November 13 body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2171: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Coe November 14, 1857, nine blocks and note fully read. Acknowledges Darwin favour of the 13th thanking for sample, suggesting earlier available beans but missing Darwin letter text. Four answers: own harvesting precludes mistake; four kinds including runner were only kinds in grounds; beans in same pod not different; dozen pure beans of each kind now enclosed. Samples came from black plant sown June and harvested autumn; several quarts reserved and separate planting next year planned. Do not activate this follow-up in Darwin same-day 2170 without receipt evidence.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
